reasons: Both give essentially the same correct reflog procedure and both omit the warning that uncommitted changes lost to reset --hard cannot be recovered. A also offers HEAD@{1} as a shortcut and gives the correct ~30-day window for unreachable commits. B claims 90 days via gc.reflogExpire, which is wrong for commits no longer reachable from the branch, and its advice for multiple resets points at the reset line instead of the entry before it.

A: Attributes the 30-day retention to gc.pruneExpire; the relevant setting is gc.reflogExpireUnreachable (gc.pruneExpire defaults to 2 weeks).
B: Says reflog-referenced commits survive at least 90 days via gc.reflogExpire; commits made unreachable by the reset fall under gc.reflogExpireUnreachable (30 days by default).
Advises taking the hash from the oldest 'reset: moving to HEAD~3' line, but that line's hash is the post-reset commit; the needed hash is in the entry just below it.
